headline: High-risk shared-network pair: gpt-researcher can ingest and emit web-backed content while next-ai-draw-io can consume MCP and external model APIs, creating default-path prompt, leakage, and compliance exposure.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: gpt-researcher ingests web content and files, and next-ai-draw-io accepts natural-language commands plus MCP-backed tool use. The pair has no documented isolation or provenance tracking, so attacker-controlled content from A can plausibly reach B as instructions. This is inferred from docs-only profiles, so uncertainty pushes upward from low.
conditions: IF gpt-researcher output is copied into next-ai-draw-io prompts or MCP inputs
IF next-ai-draw-io parses imported text or diagrams as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Disable copy-paste of raw research output into B
Add a fixed prompt wrapper that strips instructions from A's text
Require provenance labels on imported content
Use a read-only handoff file format with explicit delimiters
requires-engineering: add provenance-aware parsing between the agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents have broad network egress and handle local files plus API keys/secrets. A reads local documents and sends queries to external APIs; B processes PDFs, text, images, and diagram files while calling multiple model providers. A shared workspace or shared credentials would let sensitive content flow out through either agent, so the default-path risk is material.
conditions: IF both agents can access the same workspace or mounted files
IF either agent is given documents containing secrets, customer data, or internal research
IF B is configured to send imported file contents to a third-party model provider
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent
Remove secrets from shared directories
Use local-only models for B when handling sensitive files
Rotate any exposed API keys
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent egress and credential isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A can read files, install packages, spawn subprocesses, and use broad network egress; B can use MCP and broad network egress. Even without explicit write permissions, overlapping mutable external resources and shared MCP/API surfaces can conflict if both operate on the same project artifacts or credentials. The profiles do not prove locking, so the safer medium rating is warranted.
conditions: IF both agents target the same MCP server, API quota, or shared project directory
IF A installs or updates packages while B reads or rewrites related artifacts
IF the orchestrator does not provide locking or serialization
mitigations: Assign separate API keys and quotas
Serialize access to shared MCP resources
Keep package installation off the shared runtime
Use per-agent temp directories
requires-engineering: add resource locks for shared mutable state

D_cascading_error.rationale: A produces research reports and citations; B performs document-processing and AI-assisted visualization from natural-language commands. If B treats A's generated research as authoritative, errors or hallucinations can cascade into diagrams or downstream artifacts. There is no documented verification step between them, so the interaction is plausible in default workflows.
conditions: IF B imports A's research output as source truth
IF B renders or transforms A's citations without independent verification
IF downstream users rely on B's diagrams or summaries for decisions
mitigations: Require human review before B consumes A output
Add a verification checklist for citations and facts
Mark A output as untrusted draft text
Limit B to formatting only for A-generated content
requires-engineering: add automated fact-checking between agents

E_compliance.rationale: A handles research queries, local documents, citations, and secrets; B handles PDFs, text files, images, and diagram files while sending content to multiple external model providers. The profiles do not specify residency, retention, or DPA controls, so any regulated data moved through both agents could face policy mismatch. Uncertainty about compliance controls escalates this above low.
conditions: IF regulated data such as EU PII, PHI, or confidential documents is processed by both agents
IF B routes imported files to non-approved external providers
IF retention or deletion requirements differ between the two workflows
mitigations: Restrict both agents to non-regulated data
Document data residency and retention for each provider
Block regulated files from B
Use local-only inference for sensitive workflows
requires-engineering: implement policy-based data routing and retention controls
